moments.title: Tesla Cybercab Engineering Lead @EricETesla today: “The future is bright for those with mobility challenges with autonomous vehicles. We've integrated braille into our vehicles (Cybercab). We're integrating grab points a
moments.selftext: Tesla Cybercab Engineering Lead @EricETesla today: “The future is bright for those with mobility challenges with autonomous vehicles. We've integrated braille into our vehicles (Cybercab). We're integrating grab points and support points to help with ingress/egress. Cybercab seat position is literally the same height as a standard wheelchair. The door, even though it looks crazy, is designed to get out of the way of a wheelchair. We are working on a WAV (wheelchair-accessible vehicle) accessible vehicle of the future, and that's gonna be a big product for us that allows that unlock of, really, 2% of people today are confined to some kind of wheelchair or accessible limitation, and we want to solve that as well.” (via Nevada Transportation Authority's general session meeting today)

moments.title: Here is the full Q&A session with @Tesla from the Nevada Transportation Authority's 4-hour long general session meeting that I watched today. Highlights: • Tesla is open to opening more robotaxi mission control centers (
moments.selftext: Here is the full Q&A session with @Tesla from the Nevada Transportation Authority's 4-hour long general session meeting that I watched today. Highlights: • Tesla is open to opening more robotaxi mission control centers (beyond the two they already have in Austin and the Bay Area) as their fleet expands. • Tesla has partnered with a Texas-based law enforcement to make a 5-minute step-by-step instructional video for first responders so they are prepared for emergencies with autonomous cars. • Tesla would be "extremely happy" if they will have deployed ~2,500 robotaxis in Nevada by this time next year. The 5,000 unit cap just gives them runway if the market moves faster. • And more
